subject: trouble with new X chr permutation

messages.author: 51842bf5d091d638
messages.subject: trouble with new X chr permutation
parts:
Hello,
I am trying the new perm.Xsp=TRUE argument in scanone to find X
chromosome thresholds. I can work through the tutorial just fine so I
assume this is some problem with my data set.

What happens is that I get *fewer* permutations than I specify with
n.perm, rather than more as I would expect. For instance, if I run
200, the autosome will have 200 permuations as expected but the X chr
will have 160. The same problem occurs with the first 5 of my
phenotypes.

Thanks,
Jane Kenney-Hunt

messages.author: ab8dbe3bec292afe
messages.subject: Re: trouble with new X chr permutation
parts:
The code used to determine the number of permutations for the X
chromosome is the following:

# X chr versus autosomes
xchr <- chr.type=="X"
names(xchr) <- names(cross$geno)

# chromosome lengths
L <- summary(pull.map(cross))[,2]
L <- L[-length(L)]
La <- sum(L[!xchr])
Lx <- sum(L[xchr])

n.perm.X <- ceiling(La/Lx*n.perm)

And so, if you were doing the permutation test with just chr 19 and
X, and used n.perm=1000,
it should run 1162 permutations on the X.

karl

parts:
Chr 19 is coming out with appropriate threshold and permutation, so it
must be something with the X chr genotypes, and not the phenotypes. I
removed the wrong genotypes that the read.cross identified, and tried
running only subsets of individuals, but I'm not solving the problem.
Did anyone see anything similar that might help me identify the
problem?
Thanks,
Jane
